title: AI fabrication suspected of writing dozens of articles in Canadian publications

reading.body:
This is a case of a fabricated identity sustained across multiple publications, where an AI-generated persona was used to place opinion content in outlets that present themselves as carrying named human contributors. The failure sits at the point of contributor vetting, before publication, rather than in any single article's text. The persona operated for nearly two years and produced dozens of articles, which indicates the checks that would normally attach to a new outside writer were either absent or not applied consistently.

The impersonation was the mechanism, not a side effect. A headshot that forensic analysis found to be 97 percent AI-generated, a refusal of video calls, and a refusal of payment are all signals available to an editor at the time of onboarding. Catching this would have required verifying that the person existed independently of the material submitted, for instance through a live conversation or a check against an established identity, and treating the absence of any such contact as disqualifying rather than as an eccentricity of a contributor.

What is not established is who was behind the persona or why. Jerando's attribution to Moroccan intelligence is an allegation by an interested party, and no report here establishes the operator's identity or intent. The complaint filed in Istanbul is a complaint, not a finding, and the outlets' retractions establish that vetting failed, not that any named institution directed the operation.

reports.title: Exclusive—Fake AI columnist dupes Canadian press to target Moroccan dissidents, and a Turkish 'middleman'
Why we took down an article published under the name Daniel Robson
A statement on articles by ‘Daniel Robson’
Byline or bot? AI-generated ‘journalists’ start to appear in Canada
AI fabrication suspected of writing dozens of articles in Canadian publications

summary:
A fake AI-generated columnist named Daniel Robson infiltrated Canadian news outlets for nearly two years, publishing dozens of articles pushing pro-Morocco narratives and attacking Moroccan dissidents. The persona targeted Canadian-Moroccan businessman Hicham Jerando and former Moroccan intelligence officer Mehdi Hijaouy, and later a Turkish textile seller named Fuat, whose only connection was doing business with Jerando. Robson refused video calls and payments, and forensic analysis found his headshot was 97 percent AI-generated.

After Türkiye Today contacted Canadian outlets, the Ottawa Citizen and Policy Options deleted Robson's work, and Western Standard withdrew his articles three weeks later. Policy Options editor Les Perreaux admitted a vetting lapse. Fuat filed a complaint in Istanbul over harassment and threats, and Jerando blamed Moroccan intelligence. Retired Colonel Charles Oliviero could not confirm Robson was real.
